title: Quran Knowledge
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions about Quran revelation, familiar chapters, verses, reading habits, learning and everyday lessons. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory Quran knowledge, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages, hadith texts and Quran reference pages checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: To which prophet was the Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: Allah revealed the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.question: In which language was the Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed in Arabic. Translations help us understand its meanings.

questions.question: Which angel brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
questions.explanation: Jibril, also called Gabriel, brought the revelation by Allah's command.

questions.question: What is a chapter of the Quran called?
questions.explanation: Surah means a chapter of the Quran.

questions.question: What is a verse of the Quran called?
questions.explanation: An ayah is a verse within a surah.

questions.question: Which surah comes first in the Quran's order?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is the opening chapter in the Quran's order.

questions.question: Which surah comes last in the Quran's order?
questions.explanation: An-Nas is chapter 114, the last chapter in the Quran's order.

references.label: Quranic Arabic Corpus — Quran structure and verse numbers

questions.question: How many ayahs are in Surah Al-Kawthar?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Kawthar has three ayahs. It is a short surah.

questions.question: Whom do we ask for protection in Surah Al-Falaq?
questions.explanation: Al-Falaq teaches us to seek protection with Allah, the Lord of daybreak.

questions.question: Which pair of good qualities is taught in Surah Al-Asr?
questions.explanation: Al-Asr teaches faith, good deeds, and encouraging one another in truth and patience.

questions.question: How should we listen during our teacher's Quran recitation?
questions.explanation: The Quran teaches attentive listening. In class, we listen quietly and carefully.

questions.question: How does the Quran teach us to recite?
questions.explanation: The Quran teaches measured recitation. We give the words care instead of rushing.

questions.question: Before reciting Quran, whose protection do we seek from Shaytan?
questions.explanation: Before reciting, we ask Allah to protect us from Shaytan.

questions.question: Along with reading the Quran, what should we try to understand?
questions.explanation: Allah gave the Quran for us to think about its verses and learn from them.

questions.question: What helps us remember the Quran we have learned?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged keeping up with the Quran. Review helps us remember.

questions.question: Which two Quran activities did the Prophet ﷺ praise together?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ praised people who learn the Quran and teach it.

questions.question: A person finds Quran recitation difficult but keeps trying. What does the hadith promise?

options.text: Reward only for a beautiful voice

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ promised two rewards for someone who recites with difficulty. Keep learning with care.

questions.question: In which month was the Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: The Quran names Ramadan as the month of its revelation.

questions.question: Which prophet's story is told in Surah Yusuf?
questions.explanation: Surah Yusuf tells the story of Prophet Yusuf, also called Joseph.

questions.question: Which behavior agrees with the Quran's teaching?
questions.explanation: The Quran calls us to fairness and kindness. Its lessons guide our actions.

questions.question: What does it mean that the Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?

options.text: He wrote it from his own ideas
He copied it from a storybook

questions.explanation: The Quran is revelation from Allah, not a book the Prophet ﷺ invented.

questions.question: What is a Bangla or English translation of the Quran meant to help us do?

options.text: Replace Arabic with a new revelation

questions.explanation: A translation explains meanings in another language. The Quran's revealed language is Arabic.

questions.question: Jibril brought the Quran to the Prophet ﷺ. Where did this message come from?
questions.explanation: Jibril was the messenger bringing Allah's revelation, not its author.

questions.question: Which word means a Quran chapter?
questions.explanation: The Quran's chapters are called surahs.

questions.question: A surah contains verses. What are these verses called?
questions.explanation: Ayahs are the verses that make up a surah.

questions.question: Al-Fatihah is called the opening chapter. What does this tell us about its place in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah opens the Quran. This describes the book's order, not the order of revelation.

questions.question: What does calling An-Nas the last surah tell us?

options.text: Its place in the Quran's order
The only surah we may learn

questions.explanation: An-Nas comes last in the Quran's order. This does not mean it was revealed last.

references.label: Quranic Arabic Corpus — Quran structure and verse numbers

questions.question: Which description of Surah Al-Kawthar is correct?

options.text: A name for the whole Quran
A short surah with three ayahs

questions.explanation: Al-Kawthar is a Quran chapter with three ayahs, so it is short.

questions.question: What does seeking refuge with Allah mean?

options.text: Asking Allah for a new name
Counting how many pages we read

questions.explanation: Seeking refuge means turning to Allah for protection.

questions.question: Which reminder follows the message of Surah Al-Asr?

options.text: Help each other be truthful and patient
Pretend good deeds do not matter
Say only fast learners can do good

questions.explanation: Al-Asr teaches us to encourage one another in truth and patience, along with faith and good deeds.

questions.question: Why should we avoid talking over Quran recitation during a lesson?

options.text: To finish the lesson without listening
To make the teacher speak faster
To listen carefully to what is recited
To stop other children from learning

questions.explanation: Attentive listening shows care for the recitation and helps us follow it.

questions.question: Which reader is following the lesson of measured recitation?

options.text: One who skips every difficult word
One who changes words to finish early
One who gives each word care

questions.explanation: Measured recitation gives the words proper attention. Finishing fastest is not the goal.

questions.question: Which request seeks refuge before Quran recitation?
questions.explanation: Seeking refuge before recitation means asking Allah for protection from Shaytan. The other requests are also good duas.

questions.question: What does thinking about Quran verses help us do?

options.text: Decide which page weighs the most
Turn every lesson into a race

questions.explanation: We think about the verses to understand their lessons and take them to heart.

questions.question: Why should we revisit a surah after memorizing it?

options.text: Memorizing means we can never forget
Only new lessons are worth reading

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged regular attention to the Quran. Memorized verses need review too.

questions.question: Which activity matches the hadith about learning and teaching Quran?

options.text: Teaching words we have not checked
Learning correctly, then helping someone learn

questions.explanation: Learning and teaching Quran are both valuable. We learn carefully so we can help others correctly.

questions.question: What does the hadith about difficult recitation teach a new learner?

options.text: Difficulty does not make sincere effort worthless
Only people with perfect voices should read
A struggling learner should never try again
Reading quickly matters more than learning correctly

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages the struggling reader with reward. We keep trying and accept help to improve.

questions.question: Ramadan is the month of Quran revelation. When can we learn the Quran?

options.text: Only on the first day of Ramadan

questions.explanation: Ramadan has a special connection with the Quran. Quran learning can continue throughout the year.

references.label: Quran.com — Quran in a Year reading plan

questions.question: In the opening of Yusuf's story, to whom does he tell his dream?
questions.explanation: Early in Surah Yusuf, Yusuf tells his father about a dream he had.

questions.question: After learning that the Quran teaches kindness, what should we do?

options.text: Save kindness only for quiz time
Read the lesson but choose cruelty
Be kind only when someone gives a prize

questions.explanation: Quran lessons should shape how we behave. Kindness belongs in our daily actions.

questions.question: Sara's worksheet asks who received the Quran. Which name should she choose?
questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.question: Ayan wants to learn the Quran in its revealed language. Which class should he join?
questions.explanation: Arabic is the Quran's revealed language. A translation can help Ayan understand meanings alongside learning to read.

questions.question: A quiz asks, "Which angel brought Quran revelation?" Which name should Maryam pick?
questions.explanation: Jibril brought Allah's revelation to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.question: Your teacher says, "Open a Quran chapter." What should you look for?
questions.explanation: A surah is a Quran chapter.

questions.question: Your teacher says, "Read one Quran verse." What should you read?
questions.explanation: An ayah is one Quran verse.

questions.question: You want the opening surah in the Quran's order. Which name should you tap?
questions.explanation: Choose Al-Fatihah to open the first surah in the Quran's order.

questions.question: Hana reaches the last surah in her Quran's chapter list. Which name does she see?
questions.explanation: An-Nas is the last surah in the Quran's order, at chapter 114.

references.label: Quranic Arabic Corpus — Quran structure and verse numbers

questions.question: Your class reviews Al-Kawthar, which has three ayahs. After the third ayah, what is complete?
questions.explanation: Al-Kawthar has three ayahs. Reading all three completes that surah.

questions.question: Musa is learning Al-Falaq. Which meaning should he connect with its opening?

options.text: Describing how many pages are in the Quran
Naming the days of the week

questions.explanation: Al-Falaq opens by asking Allah, the Lord of daybreak, for protection.

questions.question: After learning Al-Asr, Salma wants to encourage her friend. Which reminder fits?

options.text: Let's hide the truth to win
Let's tell the truth and be patient
Let's tease anyone who is slow
Let's give up every good deed

questions.explanation: Encouraging truthfulness and patience puts a lesson from Al-Asr into practice.

questions.question: Your teacher starts reciting Quran during class. What should you do?

options.text: Try to drown out the recitation

questions.explanation: During the recitation, listen with attention. Save your conversation for an appropriate time.

questions.question: Omar rushes and misses words while reciting. What is the better next step?

options.text: Rush even more to catch up
Skip the rest of each verse

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches measured recitation. Slowing down helps Omar give the words proper care.

questions.question: Lina is about to recite Quran and wants to seek refuge. What should she ask Allah for?
questions.explanation: Seeking refuge turns to Allah for protection from Shaytan before reciting.

questions.question: You can recite a verse but do not understand it yet. What can help you learn its message?

options.text: Guess a meaning and teach it as certain
Ask a teacher to explain its meaning
Decide the verse has no meaning
Only look at the page number

questions.explanation: The Quran invites reflection. Ask someone knowledgeable to explain meanings you do not yet understand.

questions.question: You learned a short surah last week. What is a helpful plan today?

options.text: Promise never to read it again
Review it with a teacher or parent

questions.explanation: Regular review helps keep memorized Quran fresh. A teacher or parent can help you check it.

questions.question: Your younger sister wants to learn a surah you know well. What is a good choice?

options.text: Tell her Quran learning is only for you
Refuse because she is a beginner
Help her practice with your teacher's guidance

questions.explanation: Helping someone learn Quran is valuable. Teach carefully and ask your teacher when you are unsure.

questions.question: Zayd finds reciting difficult and feels discouraged. Which reminder follows the hadith?

options.text: Your effort matters; keep practicing with help
Only fast readers should learn Quran
A difficult word means you must quit forever
Trying has no value until you sound perfect

questions.explanation: The hadith promises reward for reciting despite difficulty. Zayd can keep practicing and learn from gentle correction.

questions.question: Ramadan has ended. What is a good choice for your Quran learning?

options.text: Put every Quran lesson away until next Ramadan
Keep a small reading and learning routine
Wait until you are an adult to return
Read only when Ramadan starts again

questions.explanation: The Quran's Ramadan connection is special. We can keep learning and reading during the rest of the year too.

references.label: Quran.com — Quran in a Year reading plan

questions.question: Your teacher asks which surah tells Yusuf's story. Which one should you open?
questions.explanation: Surah Yusuf tells Yusuf's story, beginning with his conversation with his father about a dream.

questions.question: You learn a Quran lesson about kindness. Later, a classmate drops their books. What puts the lesson into practice?

options.text: Help them pick up the books

questions.explanation: Helping a classmate is an everyday way to practice the Quran's teaching of kindness.
